passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Death of the Son.” A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon: David wrote this psalm.\r\nHe gave it to the choirmaster.\r\nHe wanted it sung to the tune called “The Death of the Son.”

passages.text: I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart; I will recount all Your wonders.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He set it to the tune called “The Death of the Son.”
David speaks to the LORD.
David gives thanks to the LORD.
He thanks the LORD with all his heart.
David remembers the LORD’s wonders.
He tells about all the LORD’s wonderful deeds.
passages.original: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ עַלְמ֥וּת לַבֵּ֗ן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ אוֹדֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל־ לִבִּ֑י אֲ֝סַפְּרָ֗ה כָּל־ נִפְלְאוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: I will be glad and rejoice in You; I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks to God.
David calls God the Most High.
David says, "I will be glad in You."
David says, "I will rejoice in You."
David says, "I will sing praise to Your name."
David praises God, the Most High.
passages.original: אֶשְׂמְחָ֣ה וְאֶעֶלְצָ֣ה בָ֑ךְ אֲזַמְּרָ֖ה שִׁמְךָ֣ עֶלְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: When my enemies retreat, they stumble and perish before You.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David has enemies.
David’s enemies turn back.
David’s enemies stumble.
David’s enemies perish.
God stands before them.
God causes their defeat.
passages.original: בְּשׁוּב־ אוֹיְבַ֥י אָח֑וֹר יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ וְ֝יֹאבְד֗וּ מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For You have upheld my just cause; You sit on Your throne judging righteously.
passages.sermon:
God is the righteous judge.
God sits on His throne.
God judges fairly.
God supports my just cause.
God upholds what is right.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עָ֭שִׂיתָ מִשְׁפָּטִ֣י וְדִינִ֑י יָשַׁ֥בְתָּ לְ֝כִסֵּ֗א שׁוֹפֵ֥ט צֶֽדֶק׃

passages.text: You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked; You have erased their name forever and ever.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and authority.
God rebukes the nations.
God destroys the wicked.
God erases the names of the wicked.
Their names are gone forever.
Their names will never return.
passages.original: גָּעַ֣רְתָּ ג֭וֹיִם אִבַּ֣דְתָּ רָשָׁ֑ע שְׁמָ֥ם מָ֝חִ֗יתָ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

passages.text: The enemy has come to eternal ruin, and You have uprooted their cities; the very memory of them has vanished.
passages.sermon:
God is the judge who sits on His throne.
God brings justice.
The enemy has suffered complete ruin.
Their destruction will last forever.
God has uprooted their cities.
No one remembers them anymore.
Their memory has vanished.
passages.original: הָֽאוֹיֵ֨ב׀ תַּ֥מּוּ חֳרָב֗וֹת לָ֫נֶ֥צַח וְעָרִ֥ים נָתַ֑שְׁתָּ אָבַ֖ד זִכְרָ֣ם הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: But the LORD abides forever; He has established His throne for judgment.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is eternal.
He lives and reigns forever.
The LORD has set up His throne.
He established His throne for judgment.
passages.original: וַֽ֭יהוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם יֵשֵׁ֑ב כּוֹנֵ֖ן לַמִּשְׁפָּ֣ט כִּסְאֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He judges the world with justice; He governs the people with equity.
passages.sermon:
The LORD judges the world.
He uses justice.
He governs all people.
He uses fairness.
passages.original: וְה֗וּא יִשְׁפֹּֽט־ תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק יָדִ֥ין לְ֝אֻמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃

passages.text: The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is a refuge.
He protects people who are oppressed.
He is a stronghold.
He gives safety in times of trouble.
passages.original: וִ֘יהִ֤י יְהוָ֣ה מִשְׂגָּ֣ב לַדָּ֑ךְ מִ֝שְׂגָּ֗ב לְעִתּ֥וֹת בַּצָּרָֽה׃

passages.text: Those who know Your name trust in You, for You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is faithful.
People who know the LORD’s name trust Him.
The LORD does not abandon those who seek Him.
The LORD keeps His promises to those who look for Him.
passages.original: וְיִבְטְח֣וּ בְ֭ךָ יוֹדְעֵ֣י שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י לֹֽא־ עָזַ֖בְתָּ דֹרְשֶׁ֣יךָ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; proclaim His deeds among the nations.
passages.sermon:
The LORD lives in Zion.
The LORD is present with His people.
Sing praises to the LORD.
Tell all nations what the LORD has done.
Proclaim His deeds everywhere.
passages.original: זַמְּר֗וּ לַ֭יהוָה יֹשֵׁ֣ב צִיּ֑וֹן הַגִּ֥ידוּ בָ֝עַמִּ֗ים עֲלִֽילוֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: For the Avenger of bloodshed remembers; He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Avenger of bloodshed.
He remembers those who suffer violence.
He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
He listens to those who are oppressed.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ דֹרֵ֣שׁ דָּ֭מִים אוֹתָ֣ם זָכָ֑ר לֹֽא־ שָׁ֝כַ֗ח צַעֲקַ֥ת עֲנִיִּים׃

passages.text: Be merciful to me, O LORD; see how my enemies afflict me! Lift me up from the gates of death, that I may declare all Your praises— that within the gates of Daughter Zion I may rejoice in Your salvation.
passages.sermon:
The speaker prays to the LORD.
The LORD is merciful.
The speaker asks the LORD for mercy.
The speaker suffers because of enemies.
The speaker asks the LORD to see this suffering.
The speaker asks the LORD to lift him up.
The speaker is near the gates of death.
The speaker wants the LORD to rescue him from death.
The speaker wants to declare all the LORD’s praises.
The speaker wants to do this in the gates of Daughter Zion.
The speaker wants to rejoice in the LORD’s salvation.
passages.original: חָֽנְנֵ֬נִי יְהוָ֗ה רְאֵ֣ה עָ֭נְיִי מִשֹּׂנְאָ֑י מְ֝רוֹמְמִ֗י מִשַּׁ֥עֲרֵי מָֽוֶת׃ לְמַ֥עַן אֲסַפְּרָ֗ה כָּֽל־ תְּהִלָּ֫תֶ֥יךָ בְּשַֽׁעֲרֵ֥י בַת־ צִיּ֑וֹן אָ֝גִ֗ילָה בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: The nations have fallen into a pit of their making; their feet are caught in the net they have hidden.
passages.sermon:
The nations made a pit.
The nations fell into that pit.
They hid a net.
Their own feet are caught in that net.
passages.original: טָבְע֣וּ ג֭וֹיִם בְּשַׁ֣חַת עָשׂ֑וּ בְּרֶֽשֶׁת־ ז֥וּ טָ֝מָ֗נוּ נִלְכְּדָ֥ה רַגְלָֽם׃

passages.text: The LORD is known by the justice He brings; the wicked are ensnared by the work of their hands. Higgaion Selah The wicked will return to Sheol— all the nations who forget God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is known for His justice.
He brings justice.
The wicked are trapped by what they have done.
Their own hands cause their downfall.
The wicked will go back to the grave.
All nations that forget God will go there too.
passages.original: נ֤וֹדַ֨ע׀ יְהוָה֮ מִשְׁפָּ֪ט עָ֫שָׂ֥ה בְּפֹ֣עַל כַּ֭פָּיו נוֹקֵ֣שׁ רָשָׁ֑ע הִגָּי֥וֹן סֶֽלָה׃ יָשׁ֣וּבוּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים לִשְׁא֑וֹלָה כָּל־ גּ֝וֹיִ֗ם שְׁכֵחֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: For the needy will not always be forgotten; nor the hope of the oppressed forever dashed.
passages.sermon:
God does not forget the needy forever.
He remembers those who are poor.
The hope of the oppressed will not be lost forever.
God will not let their hope be destroyed.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א לָ֭נֶצַח יִשָּׁכַ֣ח אֶבְי֑וֹן תִּקְוַ֥ת עֲנָוִים תֹּאבַ֥ד לָעַֽד׃

passages.text: Rise up, O LORD, do not let man prevail; let the nations be judged in Your presence.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of justice and power.
Rise up, LORD.
Do not let people win by their own strength.
Judge all the nations in Your presence.
passages.original: קוּמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אַל־ יָעֹ֣ז אֱנ֑וֹשׁ יִשָּׁפְט֥וּ ג֝וֹיִ֗ם עַל־ פָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Lay terror upon them, O LORD; let the nations know they are but men. Selah
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The psalmist speaks to the LORD.
The psalmist asks the LORD to act.
The psalmist says, "LORD, lay fear upon them."
The psalmist refers to the nations.
The psalmist wants the nations to know something.
The psalmist says, "Let the nations know they are only human."
The word "Selah" marks a pause.
passages.original: שִׁ֘יתָ֤ה יְהוָ֨ה׀ מוֹרָ֗ה לָ֫הֶ֥ם יֵדְע֥וּ גוֹיִ֑ם אֱנ֖וֹשׁ הֵ֣מָּה סֶּֽלָה׃
